faq.q: What is a Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme?
faq.a: A PLI scheme is a government program that offers financial rewards to companies for increasing their production and sales of specific goods manufactured within the country. The incentives are "linked" to their "production" performance.

faq.q: What kind of companies can benefit from the MPMS?
faq.a: Both large mobile phone manufacturers and Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) companies, as well as eligible Indian smartphone brands, can benefit if they meet the specified turnover and incremental sales criteria.

faq.q: Will mobile phones become cheaper because of this scheme?
faq.a: The scheme aims to boost local manufacturing, which can reduce costs for companies. While there's no guarantee, these cost savings can potentially lead to more competitively priced mobile phones for consumers in India.

faq.q: How does this scheme help "Make in India"?
faq.a: By offering incentives for local production, the scheme directly encourages companies to set up or expand manufacturing units in India, use more local components, and even develop products domestically, thereby strengthening the "Make in India" initiative.

faq.q: What does "incremental sales" mean in this context?
faq.a: "Incremental sales" refers to the increase in the value of goods sold by a company in a given year, compared to a pre-defined base year. The incentives are calculated on this additional sales value.
